569970:
This was recorded by holding a small PCM recorder (Zoom H1n) very close to an iPod 4th generation. The iPod was turned on and its hard drive tried to start up. You can hear the spin up of the motor and the hard drive head clicking back and forth. The hard drive fails to power up completely and eventually shuts down again.

A 350 Hz high pass filter was applied, in addition to Audacity noise reduction, to get this clean motor noise from the original recording. The stereo file was then mixed to mono because the mic was slightly off center from the iPod, and the stereo provides no benefit.

The hard drive in this iPod is a 1.8" 40 GB Toshiba hard drive, the iPod model is A1059. The microphone was held just 3 cm (1.2 in) from the iPod. Recording settings were stereo 44.1 kHz at 16 bit (WAV format). The file is the same except it's mono.

855615:
Intentional broken English language narration. Inspired by the excellent narration writing and voice performance in the 2017 PC game Bucket Detective.

Topic: Freesound moderation, dark humor.

Note: <i>I hope this text/audio isn't discouraging to you. The rant aspect serves the humor (based on "write what you know") rather than venting. Even if taken as seriously: it is okay for a volunteer moderator to feel bored sometimes while doing a task nobody is forcing them to do and they still chose to do it - that's really on the moderator. By being potentially offensive, arrogant, non self-reflective (complaining about an activity you have no obligation to do) and spoken from a privileged position the phrase aims to match the source of inspiration. It can be seen as punching down but hopefully is instead interpreted as self-deprecating through what it tells about the speaker.

Jokes really are best when explained thoroughly.</i>

Process:
- Write text. Record. Rewrite. Re-record. (Repeat as needed)
- RX Mouth De-click Sensitivity 4,0 
- Audacity Change Pitch -3 Semitones
- Audacity Change Tempo 10 Percent
- Audacity Normalize
- Dragonfly Room Reverb - Small Clear Room
- TDR Nova duck left side

Text:
<blockquote>Freesound moderating hard.
It fun because you often hear creative sounds.
But also boring hearing car drive by with wind and hand touching mic fifty times in row.
Developer team small and busy make site stable and fight spam.
Other moderators nice but you grumpy and annoy some uploaders.
You hack to make volunteer work easier.
Also write many tickets just in case devs have time one day.</blockquote>

437570:
Going through some old recordings on my hard drive.
Elastic band wrapped around a plastic filing box. The plastic box works well as a resonant body and it is possible (with a lot of practice and some luck) to scrape/rub the elastic band and get 'violin-like' sounds.

It is also necessary to experiment with the object used to scrape/rub/bow the elastic band. I tried different types of pen and settled for one that worked best. It had a very slight rough texture to improve grip and that works well to induce the rubber band to vibrate.

Short recording of scrapping sounds. Probably useless...

Recorded with Zoom H1 and home made contact mic, on 05-Jun-2011.
